summary: A scholar in religious and Buddhist studies, Edo Shonin earned a PhD from Nottingham Trent University. Affiliations attested in 2015 include research psychologist at Nottingham Trent University and Research Director at the Awake to Wisdom Centre for Meditation and Mindfulness Research.

Specializing in Buddhist and religious studies, Edoardo Siani earned an M.A. in Social Anthropology from SOAS University of London (2014–2018). He held posts at SOAS (2018–2019), Kyoto University (2018–2020), and Ca' Foscari University of Venice (assistant professor, 2020).

Edouard Müller-Hess worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Berlin, Tübingen, and Leipzig (Ph.D. 1874). He taught German at Cardiff University (1883–1888) and served as Privatdozent (1881–1883) and Professor of Sanskrit (from 1888) at the University of Bern.

A linguist who studied under Franz Bopp at Berlin (~1823–1827), Göttingen (~1827–1828), and Königsberg (Hon. Ph.D. ~1835). He held posts at the Royal Library of Berlin (1832), Prussian Academy of Sciences (1851), and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1832–1880).

A linguist who studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg from ~1847 to ~1851. Eduard Böhmer later held academic posts at Halle-Wittenberg (1859–1872) and the University of Strasbourg (~1872–1879).

A sinologist who studied at the University of Leipzig (~1910–1913) under doctoral supervisor August Conrady, whom he later succeeded. He held academic posts at Humboldt University of Berlin and the University of Leipzig (~1917–1958).

A scholar in linguistics and Indology, Hermann studied at Leipzig, Freiburg, and Jena (Ph.D. ~1891–1893 under Berthold Delbrück). He held professorships at Kiel (1913), Frankfurt (1914), and Göttingen (1917–1937), succeeding Jacob Wackernagel in 1917.

Eduard Müller was a scholar in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied under Ernst Kuhn and completed his dissertation at the University of Leipzig (~1871–1874), later serving as a professor at the University of Bern (~1886–1908).

A linguist who studied at Charles, Vienna, Chicago (M.A.), and Leipzig (Ph.D. ~1904–1905). He taught at Wisconsin-Madison (1905–1913), Texas at Austin (1913–1919), Bryn Mawr (1919–1928), and Yale as Sterling Professor of Germanic Languages (1929).

A scholar of Indology and philosophy, Röer studied at Königsberg, Jena, and Berlin (Ph.D. 1833) under Franz Bopp and J. F. Herbart. He held posts at Berlin (1833–1838), the East India Company (~1839–1861), and The Asiatic Society.

Eduard Sachau specialized in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studying at Kiel, Leipzig, and Halle (Ph.D. ~1867), he held posts at Vienna (1869), Berlin (from 1876), and the Seminar für Orientalische Sprachen (director 1887).

Schwyzer was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Leipzig and Zurich (PhD ~1893–1898 under Adolf Kaegi). He held professorships at Zurich (PD 1902; ord. Professor 1912), the University of Bonn (1927), and Humboldt University of Berlin (1932–1939).

A linguist who studied at Berlin and Leipzig (Dr. phil. 1867–1870 under Friedrich Zarncke). He was a professor at Jena (1871–1883), Tübingen (1883–1887), Halle-Wittenberg (1887–1892), and Leipzig (1892–1922).
An Indologist who studied at Basel (~1898–1902), Paris, Oxford, and Göttingen, earning his PhD in ~1902–1903 under Jacob Wackernagel.

Eduard Wölfflin was a linguist who studied at the University of Basel (~1849–1851) and the University of Göttingen (~1851–1854). He held posts at the universities of Zurich (~1861–1869), Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1869–1880), and Munich (~1880–1905).

A scholar in philosophy and religious studies, Zeller studied at the Evangelische Seminare and Tübingen (~1831–1836). He held academic posts at Tübingen (~1840–1847), Bern (~1847–1849), Marburg (~1849–1862), Heidelberg (~1862–1872), and Berlin (~1872–1895).

Eduardo Francisco Freyre Roach is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Buddhist Studies at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2014) under the supervision of Yakupitiyage Karunadasa and Georgios T. Halkias.

Eduardo Luigi De Stefani was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied under Paolo Emilio Pavolini. In 1910, he held a teaching post for Latin and Greek grammar at Sapienza University of Rome.
An Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Copenhagen, earning an M.A. in Oriental Philology (~1865–1872) under Niels Ludvig Westergaard and a Ph.D. (~1872–1879).

A scholar in philosophy and religious studies, Edvard Westermarck studied at the University of Helsinki (~1881–1889). He held academic posts at the London School of Economics (~1904–1929) and Åbo Akademi University (~1918–1932).
